cs23.document: EASA, Certification Specifications and Acceptable Means of Compliance for Normal, Utility, Aerobatic, and Commuter Category Aeroplanes, CS-23, Amendment 4, 15 July 2015 (Annex to ED Decision 2015/018/R)
cs23.why_this_one: The prescriptive CS-23 before EASA's 2017 rewrite into objective rules with consensus standards. It is the EASA text, not the FAA's; that its 23.333 and 23.341 equal 14 CFR 23.333 and 23.341 before amendment 23-64 was not checked, because no FAA text could be opened (see blocked).
cs23.opened: 2026-11-28, curl through the session proxy; text read with pdftotext -layout

gust_envelope.as_read: Positive (up) and negative (down) gusts of 50 fps at V_C at altitudes between sea level and 20,000 ft, which may be reduced linearly from 50 fps at 20,000 ft to 25 fps at 50,000 ft; positive and negative gusts of 25 fps at V_D at altitudes between sea level and 20,000 ft, which may be reduced linearly from 25 fps at 20,000 ft to 12.5 fps at 50,000 ft. (iii), 66 fps at V_B, is for the commuter category only.

gust_shape.as_read: U = (U_de/2)(1 - cos(2 pi s/(25 C))), s the distance penetrated into the gust (ft), C the mean geometric chord of the wing (ft), U_de the derived gust velocity of (c)(1); gust load factors vary linearly with speed between V_C and V_D

manoeuvre_envelope.as_read: the positive manoeuvring load factor of CS 23.337 at speeds up to V_D; the negative manoeuvring load factor of CS 23.337 at V_C; factors varying linearly with speed from the specified value at V_C to 0.0 at V_D for the normal and commuter category, and -1.0 at V_D for the aerobatic and utility categories

negative_manoeuvre_factor.as_read: the negative limit manoeuvring load factor may not be less than 0.4 times the positive load factor for the normal, utility and commuter categories

design_cruise_speed.paragraph: CS 23.335(a)(1)(i) and (a)(3), printed page 1-C-3 (PDF page 32); added 2026-11-28 after a trial run of the code, from the same opened file
design_cruise_speed.as_read: design speeds are equivalent airspeeds; V_C (in knots) may not be less than 33 sqrt(W/S) for normal, utility and commuter category aeroplanes, W/S the wing loading at design maximum take-off weight (lb/ft^2); V_C need not be more than 0.9 V_H at sea level

dive_speed.as_read: V_D may not be less than 1.40 V_C min for normal and commuter category aeroplanes

gust_load_factor.as_read: n = 1 +- k_g rho_0 U_de V a / (2 (W/S)); k_g = 0.88 mu_g/(5.3 + mu_g), the gust alleviation factor; mu_g = 2 (W/S)/(rho C a g), the aeroplane mass ratio; rho_0 sea-level density; rho density at the altitude considered; W/S the wing loading of the load case; C the mean geometric chord; V the equivalent speed; a the slope of the aeroplane normal force coefficient curve per radian (SI units in the text; the relation is dimensionless and is used here in ft, lb, s)
gust_load_factor.chord: mean geometric chord, wing area over span

factor_of_safety.as_read: unless otherwise provided, a factor of safety of 1.5 must be used

naca1206.title: A Revised Gust-Load Formula and a Re-Evaluation of V-G Data Taken on Civil Transport Airplanes From 1933 to 1950
naca1206.author: Kermit G. Pratt and Walter G. Walker, Langley Aeronautical Laboratory
naca1206.opened: 2026-11-28, curl through the session proxy (host approved by the owner); equations read from the page rendered at 250 dpi, because the text layer is a poor scan

assumptions.as_read: rigid airplane; constant forward speed; steady level flight before the gust; the airplane can rise but cannot pitch; fuselage and tail lift increments negligible beside the wing's; gust uniform across the span

equation_2.as_read: a_n(s)/a_ns + (1/mu_g) integral_0^s (1/2pi) C_L_alpha(s - s1) a_n(s1)/a_ns ds1 = integral_0^s (1/2pi) C_L_g(s - s1) d[u(s1)/U]/ds1 ds1 + (u(0)/U)(1/2pi) C_L_g(s)
equation_2.a_ns: (3): a_ns = m rho S V U/(2W), the acceleration from a steady lift at the gust's largest velocity, g units; m the wing lift-curve slope per radian
equation_2.s: distance of penetration into the gust, chords (symbols, printed p. 2); t = s c/V
equation_2.chord: c the mean geometric chord, wing area over span; the report's note says the mean aerodynamic chord may be used if used consistently (symbols, printed p. 2)

wagner.what: transient lift after a unit jump in angle of attack, normalized to 1, infinite aspect ratio (from NACA Rep. 681, R. T. Jones)
wagner.form: phi(s) = 1 - sum A_i exp(-b_i s), s in chords

kussner.what: transient lift on penetration of a sharp-edge gust, normalized to 1, infinite aspect ratio (from NACA Rep. 681)
kussner.form: psi(s) = 1 - sum A_i exp(-b_i s), s in chords

naca1206.finite_aspect_ratio_note: printed p. 3: results with these infinite-aspect-ratio functions are probably less than 5 percent different from those with finite-aspect-ratio functions (its ref. 11)

gust_shape.as_read: u(s)/U = (1/2)(1 - cos(pi s/H)) for 0 < s < 2H, 0 outside; H = 12.5 chords (the gust-gradient distance, from zero to the largest gust velocity)

gust_factor.as_read: K_g = largest a_n/a_ns over the penetration; K_g = 0.88 mu_g/(5.3 + mu_g) approximates the computed curve with an error less than +-0.01; the numerical solution has an error in a_n/a_ns less than +-0.005

figure_1.page: printed p. 4 (PDF page 7), Fig. 1, representative histories of the acceleration ratio
figure_1.read_by_eye_from_the_rendered_page: peak marks (K_g) at mu_g 3, 20 and 100 near 0.32, 0.71 and 0.84; grid lines 0.1 apart; read to about +-0.02

integration.solver: scipy.integrate.solve_ivp, method DOP853, rtol 1e-10, atol 1e-12; the gust's end (s = 2H) is a separate interval
integration.chord_for_mu: the chord Stage 1 uses in (14.8), the mean aerodynamic chord (wing.mac), so that the four mass ratios are the record's
integration.lift_slope: Stage 1's lift slope at the Mach number of V_C at each altitude (the record's gusts entries)

negative_stall.section_value_record: runs/task12/pd/2026-11-27/p2b/p2.json, measured set 2 (Re 6 million, smooth), the lowest set where the negative stall is shown
negative_stall.wing_rule: Raymer (12.15), p. 270, applied to the negative section value: 0.9 times it, quarter chord unswept (an assumption: the book states the rule for the positive stall)

choices.manoeuvre_envelope: Raymer Fig. 14.3, p. 337, and CS 23.333(b) for the normal category: the negative stall line to -1.8, flat to V_C, then linear to 0 at V_D; positive stall line to +3.8, flat to V_D

weights.zero_fuel: r0 W0 less r0 fuel (the record's convention)
weights.payload_off_no_ballast: zero-fuel weight less the 500 lb payload: hypothetical, because P4b found no layout flyable payload-off without ballast
weights.payload_off_with_ballast: zero-fuel weight less the payload plus the ballast of P4b's chosen layout (ballast_every_loading_lb, runs/task12/pd/2026-11-28/p4b/p4b.json): the operating case
weights.payload_off_full_fuel_with_ballast: take-off weight less the payload plus the same ballast

operating_limit.rule: the largest equivalent airspeed, not above V_D, at which the gust load factor under the ruled rule (30 ft/s to V_C falling to 15 ft/s at V_D) stays at or below +3.8 and at or above -1.7

row4_cases.cs23_speeds: CS 23.333(c) gust speeds (50 fps at V_C, 25 fps at V_D, full values to 20,000 ft), CS 23.341(c) formula
row4_cases.ruled_held_30: the ruled formula with the gust held at 30 ft/s above V_C (at V_D and at the level top speed)
row4_cases.weight_cost: Stage 1 (stage1.analyse, as measurement/robust_sizing.sized_aircraft_guess) at r0's L_sized with the ledger's limit_load_factor raised to the case's largest positive gust load factor at V_C and V_D (both altitudes, take-off and zero-fuel weight); the record's mission and every other ledger value unchanged

r1_findings.rule: the rows' load factors recomputed with every weight raised by the r1 empty-weight change, wing unchanged (r0 is not re-sized)
